pages.ko: 옛날 옛날 아주 먼 옛날에, 산 밑 초가집에 할머니가 혼자 살았어요. 어느 봄날 아침, 장독대 옆에서 "구렁덩덩—" 하는 소리가 났지요. 가만히 들여다보니 동글동글 조그만 구렁이 한 마리가 새근새근 낮잠을 자고 있지 뭐예요. 할머니는 구렁이를 삼태기에 살포시 담아 폭 안고 들어왔답니다.
pages.t: Long, long ago, in a thatched house at the foot of a mountain, a grandmother lived all alone. One spring morning, a sound came from beside the big clay jars in the yard — "Gureong-deongdeong—" She peeped in quietly, and what do you know: a plump little snake lay curled up there, fast asleep, breathing softly. The grandmother scooped him gently into her straw carrying basket and held him close as she brought him inside.

pages.ko: 할머니는 구렁이를 아들처럼 길렀어요. 구렁이는 삼태기 가장자리에 턱을 척 얹고 글을 읽었고, 밤이면 할머니 발치에서 도르르 몸을 말았지요. 그런데 마을 사람들은 담 밖으로 멀찍이 돌아서 다녔어요. "구렁이가 무슨 사람 노릇을 한다고!" 구렁이는 마당 끝에서 혼자 조용히 책장만 넘겼답니다.
pages.t: The grandmother raised the little snake just like a son. He would rest his chin on the rim of the straw basket and read his books, and at night he curled himself up in a coil at the grandmother's feet. But the village people always walked the long way round, keeping far outside the wall. "As if a snake could act like a person!" So out at the edge of the yard, the little snake quietly turned the pages all by himself.

pages.ko: 이웃 부잣집에는 딸이 셋 있었어요. 하루는 세 자매가 담 너머를 기웃 들여다보았지요. "으악, 징그러워!" 첫째와 둘째는 코를 막고 후다닥 달아났어요. 그런데 붉은 댕기를 드린 셋째만은 담장에 턱을 괴고 방긋 웃었답니다. "어머, 구렁덩덩 새선비네!"
pages.t: In the rich family's house next door there were three daughters. One day the three sisters peeked over the wall. "Eek, how horrid!" The eldest and the second held their noses and ran off. But the youngest, with a red ribbon in her hair, rested her chin on the wall and smiled. "Why, it's Gureong-deongdeong Saeseonbi — the little snake scholar!"

pages.ko: 그 말에 구렁이가 스르르 고개를 들었어요. "덩실덩실, 나 여기 있소!" 셋째 딸은 깔깔 웃으며 날마다 담 너머로 인사를 했지요. "구렁덩덩 새선비!" "덩실덩실, 나 여기 있소!" 그때부터 구렁이의 이름은 새선비가 되었답니다.
pages.t: At those words the snake lifted his head. "Deongsil-deongsil, here I am!" The youngest daughter laughed and laughed, and every day after that she called over the wall. "Gureong-deongdeong Saeseonbi!" "Deongsil-deongsil, here I am!" And from that day on, the snake's name was Saeseonbi.

pages.ko: 할머니는 정성껏 빚은 떡을 쪽빛 보자기에 곱게 싸서 부잣집으로 갔어요. "우리 새선비랑 한집에서 같이 사는 짝꿍이 되어 주지 않겠소?" 첫째와 둘째는 손사래를 쳤어요. "구렁이랑요? 절대 싫어요!" 그러자 셋째 딸이 조용히 앞으로 나섰지요. "저는 좋아요. 새선비는 제 동무인걸요."
pages.t: The grandmother wrapped the rice cakes she had made with such care in an indigo wrapping cloth, and went over to the rich family's house. "Won't one of you be my Saeseonbi's partner, and live together with him in one house?" The eldest and the second waved their hands. "With a snake? Never!" Then the youngest daughter quietly stepped forward. "I would like to. Saeseonbi is my friend."

pages.ko: 드디어 잔칫날! 마당에는 솔가지와 대나무를 꽂은 초례상이 차려졌어요. 새선비는 까만 사모를 반듯하게 쓰고, 셋째 딸은 붉은 댕기를 곱게 드리고 마주 섰지요. 마을 사람들이 수군수군했지만, 둘은 서로를 보고 배시시 웃었어요. 꽹과리가 꽹—꽹— 울리고 잔치가 벌어졌답니다.
pages.t: At last, the wedding day! In the yard stood the wedding table, set with pine branches and bamboo. Saeseonbi wore his black wedding hat straight and neat, and the youngest daughter tied her red ribbon on prettily, and the two of them stood face to face. The village people whispered and murmured, but those two looked at each other and smiled shyly. The little gong rang out — kwaeng, kwaeng! — and the feast began.

pages.ko: 그날 밤, 달빛이 마당 가득 쏟아졌어요. "잠깐만 눈을 감아 주오." 새선비의 몸에서 하얀 허물이 사르르 벗겨졌지요. 그러자 그 속에서 훤한 선비가 쑥 일어섰고, 벗은 허물은 하얀 나비처럼 훨훨 날아갔답니다.
pages.t: That night, moonlight poured all over the yard. "Close your eyes, just for a moment." A white skin slipped softly away from Saeseonbi's body — and up out of it rose a bright young scholar! The skin he had shed floated off, fluttering away like a white butterfly.

pages.ko: 셋째 딸은 하나도 놀라지 않았어요. 눈이 반달로 웃는 것도, 도포 자락에 남은 연둣빛 무늬도 그대로였으니까요. "새선비, 여전히 새선비네요!" 문틈으로 몰래 보던 할머니가 손뼉을 짝 쳤어요. "아이고, 우리 아들!"
pages.t: The youngest daughter was not surprised, not one bit. His eyes still smiled like two half-moons, and the soft green pattern was still there on the hem of his robe. "Saeseonbi — you're still Saeseonbi!" The grandmother, peeking through the crack in the door, clapped her hands. "Oh my goodness, my son!"

pages.ko: 이듬해 봄, 새선비는 먼 고을로 글공부를 떠나게 되었어요. 셋째 딸은 쪽빛 보자기에 봇짐을 야무지게 쌌지요. "구렁덩덩 새선비 하고 부르면, 어디서든 대답해 주세요." "그럼요. 어디에 있든 꼭 대답하지요." 두 사람은 새끼손가락을 걸었답니다.
pages.t: The next spring, Saeseonbi had to go away to a faraway town to study. The youngest daughter packed his bundle up snugly in the indigo cloth. "When I call 'Gureong-deongdeong Saeseonbi,' answer me, wherever you are." "I will. Wherever I am, I will surely answer." And the two of them hooked their little fingers together.

pages.ko: 셋째 딸이 친정에 다니러 온 날, 새선비가 돌아온다는 소식이 왔어요. 언니들은 배가 살살 아팠지요. "그 잘난 선비, 우리가 각시 노릇 좀 해 볼까?" 첫째는 셋째의 붉은 댕기를 슬쩍 빼내 제 머리에 맸어요. 둘째는 셋째를 부엌으로 살살 떠밀었지요. "너는 오늘 부뚜막이나 지키렴!"
pages.t: One day, when the youngest daughter was visiting her old home, word came that Saeseonbi was on his way back. Her sisters' stomachs began to ache with envy. "That fine grand scholar — shall we try being his bride?" The eldest slipped the red ribbon out of her sister's hair and tied it into her own. The second gave her a little push toward the kitchen. "You can mind the cooking stove today!"

pages.ko: 대문 앞에 새선비가 성큼 들어섰어요. 언니들이 앞다투어 소리쳤지요. "구렁둥둥 헌선비!" "구렁덜덜 세에선비!" 아이고, 말이 꼬여도 이렇게 꼬일 수가! 구경하던 마을 사람들이 그만 배를 잡고 웃었답니다.
pages.t: In through the front gate came Saeseonbi with long, sure steps. The two sisters called out, each trying to be first. "Gureong-dungdung Heonseonbi!" "Gureong-deoldeol Sehh-seonbi!" Oh dear — how their tongues did tie themselves in knots! The village people who had come to watch held their sides with laughing.

pages.ko: 그때 부엌문이 활짝 열렸어요. "구렁덩덩 새선비!" 맑은 목소리가 마당을 가로질렀지요. 새선비가 환하게 웃으며 대답했어요. "덩실덩실, 나 여기 있소!" 댕기가 없어도, 목소리 하나로 두 사람은 한눈에 서로를 알아보았답니다.
pages.t: Just then the kitchen door swung wide open. "Gureong-deongdeong Saeseonbi!" A clear voice rang right across the yard. Saeseonbi answered with a great bright smile. "Deongsil-deongsil, here I am!" Ribbon or no ribbon, those two knew each other at once — by nothing but a voice.

pages.ko: 언니들은 얼굴이 발그레해져 고개를 푹 숙였어요. "우리가… 미안해." 셋째 딸은 댕기를 돌려받아 다시 매고는, 두 언니의 손을 잡아 잔치 마당으로 이끌었지요. 사모를 쓴 새선비가 초례상 곁에서 껄껄 웃었고, 할머니는 삼태기 가득 떡을 담아 돌렸어요. 겉모습이 달라져도 진심은 서로를 알아본대요.
pages.t: The sisters' faces went pink and they hung their heads low. "We're… we're sorry." The youngest daughter took her ribbon back and tied it on again, then took both her sisters by the hand and led them out to the feast in the yard. Saeseonbi, in his black wedding hat, laughed beside the wedding table, and the grandmother filled her straw basket with rice cakes and passed them all around. Even when the outside changes, they say, a true heart knows its own.
